newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Booming Zimbabwe bourse expects five new listings.
newsitem.headline: Booming Zimbabwe bourse expects five new listings.

text.p: Zimbabwe's booming stock exchange is poised for intense activity in the first quarter of 1997 with five new listings in the offing, the exchange's chief executive Anthony Barfoot said on Tuesday.
The new listings would improve liquidity, but the overall number of listed companies might fall due to some planned mergers, he said.
"We've got five new listings in the pipeline and also have prospects for rights issues from now to March...We are looking at a period of intense activity," he told Reuters.
Barfoot declined to detail the planned listings but some brokers estimate that they could amount to Z$760 million (U.S.$69.7 million).
Among those in the pipeline is Zimbabwean conglomerate Trans Zambezi Industries (TZI) which is seeking to localise by March seven percent of its 46.3 million shares quoted in Luxembourg.
With an initial market capitalisation of about Z$1.8 billion (U.S.$165 million) TZI would be ranked seventh on the Zimbabwe exchange.
Two of TZI's subsidiaries, paper manufacturer and packaging firm Art Corporation and battery-maker Chloride have issued cautionary announcements of a possible offer to minority shareholders.
Other new issues in the offing include farming conglomerate CFI Holdings, variable loan company Centennial Property Holdings and plastics manufacturer Randals Holdings.
Barfoot and brokers said the current bullish sentiment on the local bourse was conducive to new listings and issues.
"The market is ripe for flotations," market analyst and columnist Beckie Masawi said, adding the market was looking attractive.

The exchange has been breaking records since the beginning of the year, driven largely by local investors fleeing the local money market where interest rates have been softening on the back of an easing in the annual inflation rate.

The main industrial index pushed through the key 10,000 psychological barrier for the first time two weeks ago, and besides a slight hiccup last week, has continued marching ahead. It closed Monday at 10,174.02.

However, Barfoot and the brokers said with a price earnings ratio of around 20, Zimbabwe had caught up with other emerging markets and foreign investors were now net sellers and this should put a cap on the market.
They also warned that fundamental economic problems that remained unresolved by President Robert Mugabe's government were likely to put breaks on the market as the year progressed.

Stockbrokers Quincor James Capel and another stockbroker said indications of a higher budget deficit than the 8.5 percent of gross domestic product forecast for the fiscal year ending June 30 might also put a damper on the market.

"With money supply growth figures obstinately in the 35 to 45 percent a year range this must put upward pressure on inflation. We don't expect further falls in the interest rate," Quincor James Capel said in its outlook for the year. ($1=Z$10.91)
